mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This effect is consistent across multiple monetary policy cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions and impending economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.3pp over 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening of consumer and residential demand, which typically triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where both HOUST and RSAFS decline by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong industrial production growth (INDPRO growth rate exceeding 1.5% annualized), the economy may be overheating, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO growth exceeds 1.5% annualized, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A strong quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) signals robust economic expansion and corporate earnings growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This effect is consistent across multiple business cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with quarterly GDP growth above 2.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in the monthly CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals heightened inflationary pressures, which typically prompts the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5pp month-over-month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong job growth (PAYEMS growth exceeding 200,000 jobs per month), the labor market is robust, signaling strong consumer spending and corporate earnings, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with PAYEMS growth exceeding 200k jobs per month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past 3 months signals an easing monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days (approximately one quarter).
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
